request.prompt: A brand-new, joyful and mesmerizing romantic theme written the way the great Tamil and Telugu film composers write the magical moment a boy sees a girl for the first time: time slows down, the whole world sparkles, his heart races with happiness. Very positive, warm, bright and dreamy from the first note to the last: a major key throughout, never sad, never melancholic, never minor. Instrumental, no lyrics. South Indian film style in the writing: a sweet singable melody in a bright raga like Mohanam or Hamsadhwani, with playful gamakam slides and sparkling grace notes on every lead, flirty question-and-answer phrases, a light swaying happy groove, a film-song interlude with flute and violin dancing around each other. About 92 BPM. A catchy five-note love hook that returns, happier each time, on a NEW lead sound every 10 seconds. Our sounds: an excited heartbeat is the kick drum, glass bangles jingling are the sparkle and shaker, a glitch-chopped veena pluck is the electronic partner of the lead, a twinkling music-box shimmer. Half warm real instruments, half soft shiny electronic colour. Timeline: 0-8 s: magic, only two sounds: a twinkling shimmer and a bright bamboo flute alone playing a rising joyful three-note call (root, major third, fifth, the last note held and bent upward), he sees her. 8-18 s: a sparkling felt piano plays the playful love hook and the glitch-chopped veena pluck answers it, stolen glances and shy smiles; a warm bright pad. 18-28 s: his heart races: the excited heartbeat kick and a happy swaying groove with hand percussion and finger snaps; the hook moves to a sweet solo violin with slides. 28-38 s: a reversed veena swell opens into pure bliss: lush bright strings and a bouncing melodic bass, the hook moves to a sweet wordless female hum answered by a smiling male hum. 38-48 s: interlude showpiece: bamboo flute and violin chase each other playfully, phrase by phrase, faster and closer, bangles as the shaker. 48-50 s: one beat where time stands still on a single twinkling note. 50-62 s: the happiest, biggest moment: the full love melody on soaring strings and a clean shimmering electric guitar, a joyful wordless chorus, the hook lifted up a whole step. 62-72 s: the flute plays the joyful three-note call once more over the shimmer and ends on one bright bell. Not sad, not melancholic, not a slow ballad, not Hollywood, not Western pop, not lo-fi, not ambient, no EDM, no white-noise risers, no side-chain pumping, no long repeats of the same sound.
